intro: Ten stories from the last day, rewritten in plain British English. Tap any word you don't know.

items.title: Two oil tankers hit mines near Strait of Hormuz
items.text: Two oil tankers hit mines and caught fire near the Strait of Hormuz, according to reports on Sunday. Fires and explosions were reported on both ships. Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy said the tankers had been using an unauthorised route with their navigation systems and AIS tracking switched off. The strait is one of the busiest shipping routes for oil in the world. Separately, the Guards said they had shot down a US MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island. Officials had not yet said whether anyone on the tankers had been hurt.

gloss.mine: a hidden bomb that explodes when a ship touches it
gloss.strait: a narrow stretch of sea between two areas of land
gloss.AIS: a system that ships use to send their position to others
gloss.shoot down: to hit an aircraft so that it falls from the sky

items.title: US air traffic control stable after nationwide outage
items.text: The US Federal Aviation Administration said air traffic control was stable again after a nationwide outage. Administrator Bryan Bedford told a news conference that the system remained stable and that airlines were recovering. He spoke alongside Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy. Airlines were expected to cancel between 4,000 and 5,000 of about 41,000 scheduled flights. Passengers across the country have faced long delays as carriers try to move planes and crews back to where they are needed.

gloss.outage: a period when a system stops working
gloss.air traffic control: the service that guides aircraft in the sky and on the ground
gloss.scheduled: planned to happen at a fixed time
gloss.cancel: to decide that a planned trip will not happen

items.title: Planning papers warn of risk at Piddington asylum camp
items.text: A government planning document for an asylum camp at the Ministry of Defence site near Piddington in Oxfordshire says safety measures cannot eliminate all risk, according to GB News. The plan has attracted 3,177 objections during public consultation. Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp accused Labour of abusing its emergency powers to approve the camp. About 20 local women have signed up for self-defence classes. The Government has not been quoted in the report seen here.

gloss.asylum: protection given to people who have left their own country because of danger
gloss.consultation: a period when the public can give opinions on a plan
gloss.object to: to say that you disagree with or oppose something
gloss.emergency powers: special legal powers a government can use in urgent situations
gloss.sign up for: to put your name down to join something

items.title: Denmark beat Ronaldo-less Portugal 4-1
items.text: Denmark won 4-1 in Braga in the Nations League, in Portugal's first match since Cristiano Ronaldo retired from international football. Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg scored a penalty in the 43rd minute after a handball by Ruben Dias. Rasmus Hojlund then scored twice, and Joachim Andersen added a header. Bernardo Silva scored Portugal's only goal. Portugal had already reached the quarter-finals. Denmark will go through if they draw at Norway on Tuesday.

gloss.penalty: a free shot at goal given after a foul in the box
gloss.handball: a foul when a player touches the ball with a hand or arm
gloss.header: a goal scored with the head
gloss.quarter-final: a match in the last eight of a competition
gloss.go through: to move on to the next stage

items.title: Haaland sets Nations League goal record
items.text: Erling Haaland scored a late penalty as Norway beat Wales 3-1 in Oslo. It was his 23rd goal in the Nations League, a competition record. Antonio Nusa gave Norway the lead just before the hour and Oliver Schjelderup added a second. Brooks scored a goal for Wales. Wales are expected to finish bottom of Group A4 and face possible relegation to League B. Norway play Denmark on Tuesday.

gloss.relegation: moving down to a lower division
gloss.late: near the end of a match

items.title: SpaceX catches Starship upper stage with tower arms
items.text: SpaceX has caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket using the robotic arms of its launch tower in Texas. The stage returned after a mission of more than 22 hours. Anadolu Agency described it as the first time an upper stage coming back from orbit has been caught by a tower. Catching rockets in this way is meant to let the company use them again quickly. Starship is the vehicle SpaceX hopes to use for flights to the Moon and Mars.

gloss.upper stage: the top part of a rocket that goes into space
gloss.robotic: controlled by a machine, not a person
gloss.orbit: the curved path around the Earth
gloss.launch tower: a tall structure that supports a rocket before and after flight

items.title: Study: drugs, diet and exercise slow biological ageing
items.text: Researchers at Yale have found that some medicines, healthy diets and exercise can reduce biological age. The team reviewed 51 clinical studies and looked at more than 110 DNA biomarkers in Nature Medicine. Metformin, semaglutide and anti-TNF therapies showed the strongest effects. Mediterranean, low-fat and low-carb diets also helped. Over-the-counter supplements showed no measurable benefit. The authors said it is not yet proven that a lower biological age leads to a longer or healthier life.

gloss.biological age: how old your body seems from its cells, not from your birthday
gloss.biomarker: a measurable sign in the body that shows what is happening inside it
gloss.clinical study: research that tests treatments on people
gloss.measurable: big enough to be counted or measured

items.title: Philippines wins first Eurovision Song Contest Asia
items.text: The Philippines has won the first Eurovision Song Contest Asia. Nineteen-year-old Carmelle won in Bangkok with the song Sobra-Sobra. She scored 211 points, including 93 from the juries and 118 from viewers at home. Ten other Asian countries took part in the contest. The event follows the format of the long-running European competition, in which countries send singers to compete in a live television final.

gloss.jury: a small group of experts who judge a contest
gloss.take part: to join an activity with others
gloss.format: the way an event is organised
gloss.compete: to try to win against others

items.title: Italy fines Meta 805 million euros over Android data
items.text: Italy's data protection authority has fined Meta 805 million euros, about 900 million dollars. The regulator said the company had accessed photos, videos and metadata on Android devices without specific, informed consent from users. Metadata is information about files, such as when and where a picture was taken. The fine is one of the largest of its kind in Europe. Meta has not been quoted in the report seen here.

gloss.fine: to make someone pay money as a punishment
gloss.regulator: an official body that checks that companies follow the rules
gloss.metadata: data that describes other data, such as the date of a photo
gloss.authority: an official organisation with legal power

items.title: GTA VI launches on Thursday after record preorders
items.text: Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on 19 November on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S, thirteen years after its predecessor. Sensor Tower estimates about 12.1 million digital preorders worth roughly 1.18 billion dollars. Rockstar opened the 212 GB preload last week and is not making discs. It will offer a free printable poster and a map of Leonida on launch day. Several publishers have moved their releases away from the date.

gloss.preorder: an order for a product before it is on sale
gloss.preload: to download a game before its official release
gloss.predecessor: the earlier thing in a series
gloss.move away from: to change a date so it does not clash with something else
gloss.launch: the start of selling a product
